mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25 percentage points above its prior month, it anticipates reduced near-term discounting of corporate cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than 0.5% with p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior month's level, accompanied by UNRATE below 7%, signals labor market softening that supports equity risk appetite and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS growth is not followed by SPX 20d returns exceeding 1%, with p-value > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in both HOUST (residential construction) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels indicates strengthening demand, which predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day returns do not exceed the 5-day average by more than 2% with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% suggests supply-side weakness, which, when combined with a 20-day negative S&P 500 return, implies a negative 20-day forward return as investors discount future earnings.
failure_condition: Over 20 days, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during INDPRO declines > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month, it signals inflation expectations rising, which typically precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion increases.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during such CPI movements.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in UNRATE below 5% indicates weaker wage pressures, which, when combined with a 60-day horizon, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return as uncertainty diminishes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not beat the 20-day average by more than 0.5% with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly declines in GDPC1 (GDP) and PAYEMS suggest economic contraction, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as risk aversion rises.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during such dual declines.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO remains flat for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS is above 1%, it suggests supply-side constraints persist under looser policy, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) in such regimes.
